- When sentiment is consistently neutral or negative (0.00), model tends to overestimate prices in early forecast periods; correct by reducing initial forecast values by 1–2%.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >10% from prior period), model often overshoots in the next 5–7 days; apply a 5–10% downward correction to subsequent forecasts.
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days of price decline after peak), model tends to hold or overestimate; reduce forecast by 1–3% per day of deviation.
- In low-sentiment periods, model often fails to capture downward momentum; add a 0.5–1.5% drag to forecast if price drops >1% from prior day.
- For 30-day horizon, model frequently overestimates near the end of the forecast window; apply a 1–2% downward adjustment to final 5–7 days if sentiment remains flat or negative.
- If sentiment history includes a single positive signal (e.g., 0.25), model may overreact; reduce forecast by 1–2% for the next 3–5 days unless confirmed by additional signals.
